title: Boolean target_gb is accepted as zero and plans deletion of every failure artifact
observed_behavior: The strict route payload leaves target_gb typed as Any, the facade converts JSON booleans with float(), and False becomes 0.0 without an error. Because an explicit zero target intentionally enables target cleanup, the plan selects every regular file under the current and legacy failure-artifact roots. A confirmed policy cleanup does not require the preview fingerprint used for explicit artifact_paths.
expected_invariant: Numeric deletion-policy overrides must reject JSON booleans and other non-numeric types before planning; a type mistake must never broaden a confirmed cleanup to all retained failure artifacts.
root_cause: The numeric override parser relies on Python float() without first excluding bool, even though bool is a subclass of int. The downstream policy interprets an explicit zero as an enabled clean-to-zero request.
failure_scenario: A Local API caller submits target_gb=false, for example through malformed UI state or an integration client, together with dry_run=false and confirm_delete=true. Request validation accepts it as 0 GB, the backend current-plan mode selects all failure artifacts, and the cleanup permanently unlinks evidence files while reporting a valid confirmed policy cleanup.
evidence: FailureArtifactCleanupCommandPayload declares target_gb as Any while its confirmation fields are strict booleans.
_failure_artifact_cleanup_override calls float(request.get(key)); float(False) is 0.0 and returns no validation error.
failure_artifact_cleanup_policy treats target_gb is not None as an explicit override and enables target cleanup when the explicit value is zero.
failure_artifact_cleanup_plan subtracts oldest files until current_bytes <= target_bytes; with target_bytes=0 it plans every scanned artifact.
A temporary two-file reproduction returned override_value=0.0, override_error=None, target_enabled=true, and planned_count=2 without deleting any file.
affected_flows: failure artifact retention and disk-pressure cleanup
operator diagnostic and recovery evidence preservation
existing_safeguards: Live cleanup still requires dry_run=false and confirm_delete=true as exact JSON booleans.
Deletion is restricted to regular non-symlink files beneath backend failure-artifact roots.
Explicit artifact_paths cleanup requires a matching dry-run fingerprint and a manifest records attempted deletions.
safeguard_gap: Confirmation proves intent to run the supplied policy, but the supplied policy is misparsed. Policy-based current-plan cleanup deliberately does not require a dry-run fingerprint, so no lower layer distinguishes false from an intentional numeric zero.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_failure_markers.py covers numeric retention/target cleanup plans and selected-path fingerprint behavior.
tests_missing: Negative strict-contract and facade tests for boolean retention_days and target_gb
Confirmed current-plan test proving invalid numeric types cannot become a delete-all target
recommended_remediation: Reject isinstance(value, bool) before numeric conversion, type target_gb and retention_days with strict numeric Pydantic fields, and add table-driven negative route/facade tests for booleans, strings, NaN, and infinity. Preserve intentional numeric zero only when it arrives as an actual JSON number.
remediation_risk: Medium: zero is an intentional clean-all target and must remain available to explicitly numeric callers; avoid weakening the root, symlink, confirmation, manifest, or selected-path fingerprint controls.
validation_rung: Run focused failure-artifact contract, facade, planning, boundary, and cleanup tests with temporary artifact roots. No application launch or real media is required.
prior_audit_relationship: The archived W06 strict-confirmation finding was fixed for its named confirmation fields. This is a distinct current defect in a destructive numeric policy override added to the same Local API boundary.

title: A failed GPU probe is forgotten on the next cycle while stale cached utilization is presented as current
observed_behavior: After at least one successful nvidia-smi sample, a due probe failure reports an error for that single snapshot but leaves _last_gpu_rows intact. The next 2-second sampler cycle is inside the 12-second sub-cadence, reapplies those old rows to a new snapshot, and emits no error or stale marker. Repeated due-probe failures can therefore show an old GPU/NVENC percentage as freshly sampled for most cycles indefinitely.
expected_invariant: Cached telemetry reused after a failed refresh must retain its original sample time and degraded/stale error state, or be cleared; a failed authoritative probe must not be followed by an apparently fresh error-free projection of older values.
root_cause: The due-probe path advances _last_gpu_sample_at before probing but neither clears nor marks _last_gpu_rows on timeout, nonzero exit, malformed output, or exception. The cache-hit path copies old rows into a new TelemetrySnapshot without carrying a cache timestamp or last probe error.
failure_scenario: nvidia-smi succeeds once, then the driver or executable begins failing. The due cycle briefly reports the failure, but every intermediate sampler cycle until the next due probe reports the last successful encoder utilization under a new collected_at time with source=nvidia-smi and error blank. If failures persist, the misleading pattern repeats after every due probe.
evidence: The cache-hit branch applies _last_gpu_rows whenever now - _last_gpu_sample_at is below 12 seconds and does not set snapshot.error or any stale field.
The due branch sets _last_gpu_sample_at before run_capture, but failure branches only set the current snapshot error and do not invalidate or annotate _last_gpu_rows.

A read-only synthetic reproduction seeded a 77% cached row, forced a due nonzero nvidia-smi result, then sampled one second later: the failed snapshot contained driver unavailable, while the next snapshot contained next_error='', next_gpu=77.0, and next_source='nvidia-smi'.
affected_flows: GPU/NVENC operational diagnosis during driver or nvidia-smi failure
existing_safeguards: A due probe timeout, parse failure, nonzero exit, stderr result, or exception is reported on the snapshot produced by that due cycle.
GPU process spawning is bounded to the 12-second sub-cadence.
safeguard_gap: The failure evidence is ephemeral for one 2-second snapshot while the retained data has no source sample timestamp, age, or degraded-cache marker; normal UI polling can miss the failure and see only stale data labeled as current.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_telemetry_service.py covers successful cache reuse and isolated malformed/nonzero probe failures.
tests_missing: Sequential success, due failure, then cache-hit coverage
Persistent probe-failure coverage asserting timestamp/error/staleness behavior
recommended_remediation: Store cached GPU rows together with their successful sample timestamp and last probe error. On a failed due refresh, either invalidate the cache or reuse it only with explicit stale/degraded metadata and the original sample time until a successful probe replaces it. Add the sequential regression cases.
remediation_risk: Low: preserve the process-spawn sub-cadence and successful cache reuse; only degraded-cache evidence and invalidation semantics need to change.
validation_rung: Run focused telemetry-service and telemetry-contract tests with mocked nvidia-smi results. No application launch, GPU hardware, or real media is required.
prior_audit_relationship: No current or archived W06 finding covered telemetry cache degradation after a successful sample.

category: strict numeric configuration and encode waste-guard policy
title: Eight encode-waste numeric fields omit boolean rejection, allowing JSON booleans to become policy thresholds
observed_behavior: All eight integer EncodeWasteGuard threshold, cadence, and sample fields are absent from NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS, so the Config before-validator does not apply the repository's boolean-numeric rejection to them. Pydantic then coerces bound-valid JSON booleans into integers: false becomes 0 for the three zero-allowed thresholds, and true becomes 1 for those thresholds plus ConsecutiveSamples, PollSeconds, and PreflightSampleCount. The settings validator performs its explicit integer checks only after this contract normalization, so those six combinations have no field-specific error.
expected_invariant: Every persisted numeric config field must reject JSON booleans before Pydantic integer coercion, especially fields that control an enforce-mode early termination policy for active encodes.
root_cause: Strict numeric behavior depends on the hand-maintained NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS registry. The eight EncodeWasteGuard integer fields were added to Config and the downstream numeric policy but not to that registry, and no completeness check compares the registry with numeric model fields.
failure_scenario: A settings client submits true for EncodeWasteGuardMinProgressPercent, MinElapsedSeconds, OversizeMarginPercent, ConsecutiveSamples, or PollSeconds while EncodeWasteGuardMode is enforce. The saved values become 1, allowing the engine to consider stopping an active encode after about one percent progress, one elapsed second, a one-percent oversize margin, one sample, and one-second polling. False is also accepted as zero for the three zero-allowed thresholds.
evidence: Config._reject_boolean_numeric_fields delegates exclusively to NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS before normal Pydantic field parsing.
The eight EncodeWasteGuard integer fields are declared at config.py lines 143-150, while none appears in the complete NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS tuple at config_fields.py lines 505-586.
A model-field inventory found 88 numeric Config fields and 80 registry members; the exact eight-field difference is the EncodeWasteGuard numeric group.

A corrected bundled-Python reproduction showed MinProgress, MinElapsed, and OversizeMargin accept false as 0 and true as 1; ConsecutiveSamples, PollSeconds, and PreflightSampleCount accept true as 1. Bound-invalid boolean combinations were rejected only incidentally by ge constraints.

The settings validation flow first model-validates and dumps normalized Python values, then applies validate_required_and_numeric_config, so its isinstance(bool) guard sees integers rather than the original JSON booleans.
affected_flows: settings validation, preview, and confirmed save
PSD1/JSON settings authority load and migration
PowerShell encode-size waste guard preflight and active encode enforcement
existing_safeguards: Pydantic ge/le bounds reject boolean values when their coerced 0 or 1 falls outside a field's allowed interval.
EncodeWasteGuardMode defaults to off and must be explicitly set to enforce for active early termination.
Settings save requires strict confirmation and review evidence.
safeguard_gap: Confirmation and bounds validate the post-coercion numeric policy, not the caller's original type. Six bool/value combinations are valid integers after coercion, and enforce mode intentionally trusts those thresholds.
tests_present: Config and settings validation tests cover strict boolean rejection for numeric fields already listed in NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS and cover ordinary encode-waste numeric bounds.
tests_missing: Completeness assertion that every numeric Config field is in the strict-numeric registry
Boolean input cases for each EncodeWasteGuard integer field through Config and the settings save-validation path
recommended_remediation: Add all eight EncodeWasteGuard numeric keys to NUMERIC_CONFIG_KEYS and add a schema/model-driven completeness regression test so future numeric fields cannot bypass the before-validator. Preserve the existing bounds and add table-driven false/true rejection tests through the public settings validation path.
remediation_risk: Low: correctly typed integer settings remain unchanged; existing persisted boolean values, if any, will become validation errors and should be surfaced with actionable migration evidence rather than silently coerced.
validation_rung: Run focused config contract, generated schema/mirror check, settings validation/save, and encode-waste policy tests with temporary config paths. No application launch or real media is required.
prior_audit_relationship: No archived W06 finding covered strict numeric registry completeness or encode-waste guard settings.

category: copy transaction concurrency and stale-artifact cleanup
title: Stale cleanup can recursively delete a live Robocopy staging tree

locations.symbol: Copy-FileRobocopy active transaction staging and polling

observed_behavior: Copy-FileRobocopy writes each active transfer beneath a shared .mediapipeline-staging root, but both failure cleanup and startup stale cleanup infer liveness only from directory LastWriteTime. The startup path recursively removes the entire staging root once that directory timestamp is older than CleanupStaleAgeHours, without examining current child-file writes, transaction ownership, a heartbeat, a lock, or active process evidence. The copy failure path similarly deletes any sibling transaction directory older than 24 hours.
expected_invariant: Cleanup must never remove a staging tree owned by a live copy transaction. Age-based recovery must be transaction-scoped and require affirmative expired-or-terminal evidence, not a parent-directory timestamp that active file-content writes do not refresh.
root_cause: The staging protocol creates unique GUID directories but persists no owner/lease/heartbeat state. Cleanup treats directory modification time as a liveness proxy even though writing bytes to an existing child file updates the file timestamp, not the parent or staging-root timestamp.
failure_scenario: A large local, mapped-drive, explicitly enabled remote, or parallel-worker Robocopy remains active beyond the configured one-hour minimum cleanup age or the hard-coded 24-hour sibling threshold. Another startup or failed concurrent copy runs cleanup, recursively deletes the live staging root/directory, and the active transfer or subsequent atomic landing fails and retries after hours of wasted work. The original source and prior destination remain protected, but work availability and completion evidence are lost.
evidence: Copy-FileRobocopy lines 516-576 creates a GUID child and runs the bounded Robocopy process while polling the landed file.
Lines 659-665 enumerate and recursively remove sibling transaction directories older than 24 hours without transaction ownership or active-process checks.
Clear-StalePartialFiles lines 829-845 matches only the literal .mediapipeline-staging name, compares that directory's LastWriteTime to the configurable cutoff, and recursively deletes the whole tree.
The config permits CleanupStaleAgeHours as low as one hour and RobocopyTimeoutSeconds as high as 172800 seconds, so the cleanup and active-copy windows overlap by design.

A disposable current-filesystem probe created an old staging directory with a fresh actively appended child file; after the append the staging directory still satisfied the one-hour stale predicate while the child file had the current timestamp.
Current path-boundary tests prove old empty staging directories are removed and fresh roots preserved, but do not place a fresh or open transaction inside an old staging root.
affected_flows: startup and failure recovery on local, mapped, or cleanup-enabled remote roots
existing_safeguards: Each copy uses a unique GUID child directory and partial/backup leaf names.
Destination and staging paths are boundary-validated before creation.
Destination replacement is atomic and the original source is read-only.
Remote stale cleanup is disabled by default for UNC paths.
Copy failure is retried and does not authorize downstream processing.
safeguard_gap: Unique names prevent collisions but do not prove liveness; boundary guards constrain where deletion occurs but not whether the targeted transaction is active. Mapped network drives are not UNC strings, remote cleanup can be enabled, and local parallel or separately launched processes can share the same configured staging root.
tests_present: Invoke-PathBoundaryGuardChecks.ps1 covers exact generated names, old empty versus fresh staging roots, unsafe destinations, low-space preflight, and stop-before-copy cleanup.
Scratch identity and pending-publish fault suites prove source preservation and downstream fail-closed behavior after copy failure.
tests_missing: Old staging root containing a fresh or open actively written transaction must be preserved.
Parallel copy where one failure cleanup cannot delete the other transaction.
Long-copy heartbeat/lease expiry and restart recovery.
Mapped-drive and explicitly enabled remote cleanup concurrency cases.
recommended_remediation: Persist a transaction-scoped owner/run ID and heartbeat or lease inside each GUID directory, refresh it while Robocopy runs, and delete only individual transactions whose lease is expired and whose owning process/run is terminal. Never recursively delete the shared staging root based solely on its timestamp; preserve unknown/nonconforming contents for review.
remediation_risk: Medium-high: cleanup and copy landing are high-risk filesystem paths. Changes must preserve boundary validation, source immutability, atomic replacement/rollback, stop handling, and recovery of genuinely abandoned artifacts.
validation_rung: Add synthetic concurrent-copy and long-running heartbeat fault injection, existing path-boundary and pending-publish transaction suites, reliability regression, and representative mapped/UNC copy validation before release. No real media was used to establish this finding.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding covered directory-age cleanup racing a live copy transaction; W04-005 concerns destination-lock identity during pending drain and does not protect this shared staging cleanup.
